newsitem.title: UK: Shell talks with Bechtel for share of power firm.
newsitem.headline: Shell talks with Bechtel for share of power firm.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group said on Thursday it was in talks with U.S. engineers Bechtel to take a 50 percent share in the company's power generating subsidiary International Generating Company (InterGen).
Shell subsidiary Shell International Gas Ltd was aiming to complete negotiations with Bechtel by the end of September, Shell said in a release.
A company spokesman declined comment on the likely cost of the purchase.

The partnership would give Shell a share in four power projects under construction -- in Britain, the Philippines, Mexico, and Colombia -- totalling 2,145 megawatts and contracts or mandates for an additional seven projects totalling 4,275 megawatts.
Additionally Intergen has more than 20 other generating projects totaling 10,000 megawatts in various stages of development in addition to pipeline, fuels trading and gas storage activities.
The deal would represent a significant step forward for Shell in its ambitions to become an international player in the power generating sector.
Shell said earlier this year it planned a major move over the next five years into world electricity markets.
The company already has independent projects underway in the Philippines, Namibia and Peru.
Bechtel, based in San Francisco, is one of the world's leading engineering, construction and project management companies.
It has built more than 450 power stations across the globe worth more than 250,000 megawatts of generating capacity.
